records.source: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.
records.gloss: At that the time went the Jesus on the Sabbaths through the grainfields; the and disciples of him were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
pieces: About that time Jesus was walking through the fields of grain on a Sabbath day. His disciples were hungry, so they started picking some heads of grain and eating them.

L.1: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath; and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.

R.1: Around that time, Jesus was walking through some grain fields on the Sabbath, the day of rest. His followers were hungry. So they began to pick some grain and eat it.

decisions.choice: plucking grain: allowed in a neighbor's field, but counted as work on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law let a hungry traveler pick grain by hand in someone else's field (Deuteronomy 23:25). The question is the day: harvesting was forbidden on the Sabbath (Exodus 34:21), and plucking could be counted as harvesting.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: at that time: the scene follows Jesus's promise of rest (11:28-30)
decisions.reason: Matthew joins the Sabbath stories to the call to find rest in Jesus. The link is one of placement, not of time.

decisions.choice: the day of rest
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sabbath is.

records.heading: Lord of the Sabbath

records.source: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.
records.gloss: The but Pharisees having seen said to him, Look, the disciples of you are doing what not is lawful to do on Sabbath.
pieces: The Pharisees saw it and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "See there! Your disciples are doing something that the law forbids on the Sabbath."

L.2: But the Pharisees, seeing [this], said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on [the] Sabbath."

R.2: Some Pharisees saw this. They said to Jesus, "Look! Your followers are doing something that is against the law on the Sabbath."

decisions.choice: not lawful: forbidden by the law as the Pharisees understood it
decisions.reason: The Pharisees counted plucking grain as the work of harvesting, which the law of Moses forbade on the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); see there (B)
decisions.reason: In speech the word points to something happening in front of them, so it is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: He but said to them, Not have you read what did David when he was hungry and those with him?
pieces: Jesus answered them, "Do you not remember reading what David did when he and the men with him were hungry?

L.3: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him?

R.3: Jesus answered, "Have you not read about what David did when he and his men were hungry?

decisions.choice: what David did: 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: David, fleeing from Saul, asked the priest at Nob for bread and was given the holy bread.

decisions.choice: have you not read: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The Pharisees knew the Scriptures well. Jesus asks whether they have understood what they read.

records.source: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγον, ὃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;
records.gloss: how he entered into the house of the God and the loaves of the presentation they ate, which not lawful was for him to eat nor for those with him, except for the priests only?
pieces: He went into the house of God, and they ate the sacred bread set out before God. Neither David nor his men were allowed to eat it; only the priests were.

L.4: How he entered the house of God, and they ate the loaves of the presentation, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?

R.4: David went into the house of God, and they ate the special bread that had been placed there before God. The law did not allow David or his men to eat that bread. Only the priests were allowed to eat it.

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the twelve loaves set out before God
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were placed on a table in the holy place each Sabbath and were afterward eaten only by the priests (Leviticus 24:5-9; Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tabernacle, then at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple had not yet been built. The tent of meeting stood at Nob (1 Samuel 21:1).

decisions.choice: they ate, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he ate, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he ate". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: The verse continues the question of 12:3. Balanced and Readable tell the story as statements so it is easy to follow.

records.source: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;
records.gloss: Or not have you read in the law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple the Sabbath profane and guiltless are?
pieces: Or have you not read in the law that every Sabbath the priests working in the temple break the Sabbath, and still they bear no guilt?

L.5: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?

R.5: And have you not read in the Law of Moses that the priests work in the temple on the Sabbath? They break the Sabbath rules, but God does not count them guilty.

decisions.choice: the priests' Sabbath work: the offerings and the holy bread
decisions.reason: The law required extra offerings on the Sabbath (Numbers 28:9-10), and the holy bread was set out every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:8). The priests worked so that this could be done.

decisions.choice: profane: treat as ordinary, by doing work the day otherwise forbids
decisions.reason: The priests do not despise the Sabbath. They do on it what would be work on any other day.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: God does not count them guilty
decisions.reason: Readable says who holds them innocent: the law God gave.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.
records.gloss: I say but to you that the temple greater is here.
pieces: I tell you, here is something greater than the temple.

L.6: But I tell you that [something] greater than the temple is here.

R.6: But I tell you, something more important than the temple is here with you now.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: The neuter points to Jesus and what God is doing through him, which is greater than the temple and its service. If priests serving the temple are guiltless, so are those who serve him.

decisions.choice: here with you now
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "here" means in their presence.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.
records.gloss: If but you had known what is, Mercy I desire and not sacrifice, not would you have condemned the guiltless.
pieces: If you had understood what the words mean, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned people who have done nothing wrong.

L.7: But if you had understood what this is, 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned those who are guiltless.

R.7: The Scriptures say, 'I want you to show mercy to people, more than I want you to offer sacrifices.' If you had understood what that means, you would not have judged these innocent men to be guilty.

decisions.choice: I desire mercy, not sacrifice: Hosea 6:6, quoted already in 9:13
decisions.reason: God wants faithful love more than offerings. The "not" ranks the two. The wording is kept the same as in 9:13 at each level.

decisions.choice: the guiltless: the disciples
decisions.reason: The same word described the priests in 12:5. The disciples are as innocent as they are.

decisions.choice: the quotation first, then the condition
decisions.reason: Readable gives the Scripture before saying what they failed to understand.

records.source: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
records.gloss: Lord for is of the Sabbath the Son of the Man.
pieces: For the Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath."

L.8: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."

R.8: The Son of Man is the Lord who rules over the Sabbath day."

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: Jesus has authority over the day God gave
decisions.reason: God made the Sabbath holy (Exodus 20:8-11). The Son of Man has the right to say what the day allows.

decisions.choice: Lord: placed first in the sentence for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "Lord" at the head of the sentence.

records.source: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν·
records.gloss: And having moved on from there he came into the synagogue of them;
pieces: Jesus left that place and went into their synagogue.

L.9: And moving on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into their synagogue.

R.9: Then Jesus went on from there and entered their synagogue, the place where people met to worship.

decisions.choice: their synagogue: the synagogue of the people of that place
alternatives: a synagogue belonging to the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Matthew often says "their synagogues" (4:23; 9:35). The Pharisees of 12:2 are present there (12:14).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Doing good on the Sabbath

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν.
records.gloss: And behold, a man a hand having withered.
pieces: A man was there whose hand was shriveled.

L.10: And look, [there was] a man having a withered hand.

R.10: There was a man there with a hand that was shriveled and useless.

decisions.choice: withered: dried up and shrunken, so that it could not be used
decisions.reason: The word means dry. It is used of a hand that cannot move (1 Kings 13:4).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστι τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύειν;
records.gloss: And they asked him saying, If it is lawful on the Sabbaths to heal?
pieces: They put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Is healing allowed on the Sabbath?"

L.10: And they questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"

R.10: Some Pharisees were there. They asked Jesus, "Does our law allow anyone to heal on the Sabbath?"

decisions.choice: if: here it introduces a direct question
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time the word for "if" can begin a question.

decisions.choice: healing on the Sabbath: debated
alternatives: clearly forbidden by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law of Moses does not mention healing on the Sabbath. Later Jewish teaching allowed it when a life was in danger; this man's life was not.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: Some Pharisees
decisions.reason: The questioners are the Pharisees, as 12:14 shows. Readable names them.

records.source: ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: so that they might accuse him.
pieces: They wanted a reason to bring a charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.10: They were hoping to find a reason to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: accuse: bring a formal charge
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing a charge before judges. Breaking the Sabbath was a serious offense under the law (Exodus 31:14).

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίς ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;
records.gloss: He but said to them, What man will be of you who will have sheep one, and if falls this on the Sabbaths into a pit, not will take hold of it and raise?
pieces: He answered them, "Suppose one of you has just one sheep, and it falls into a hole on the Sabbath. Will you not grab hold of it and pull it out?

L.11: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What {{gender:person|man}} will there be among you who has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift [it] out?

R.11: Jesus said to them, "Suppose one of you has only one sheep, and it falls into a deep hole on the Sabbath. You will surely grab it and pull it out.

decisions.choice: rescuing an animal on the Sabbath: what his hearers would do
alternatives: a rule all Jews agreed on
decisions.reason: Jewish groups disagreed about this. The Damascus Document found at Qumran forbids lifting an animal out of a pit on the Sabbath. Jesus appeals to what his hearers themselves would do.

decisions.choice: one sheep: perhaps the only one the man owns
alternatives: one sheep out of a flock
decisions.reason: The number stresses how much the loss would matter to him.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Will you not lift it out?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

records.source: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου.
records.gloss: By how much then is worth more a man than a sheep.
pieces: And a human being is worth far more than a sheep!

L.12: How much more valuable then is a human being than a sheep!

R.12: And a person is worth much more than a sheep!

decisions.choice: an exclamation, from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates it as a statement. If a sheep may be rescued, how much more a person (6:26; 10:31).

records.source: ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.
records.gloss: So that it is lawful on the Sabbaths well to do.
pieces: So the law allows doing good on the Sabbath."

L.12: So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."

R.12: So the law allows people to do good things on the Sabbath."

decisions.choice: to do good: to act rightly and help others
decisions.reason: The phrase means to do what is right and kind, here by healing.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

records.source: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.
records.gloss: Then he says to the man, Stretch out of you the hand; and he stretched out, and it was restored healthy as the other.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and it was made well again, just like his other hand.

L.13: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched [it] out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.

R.13: Then Jesus said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held out his hand, and it became healthy again. It was just like his other hand.

decisions.choice: it was restored: God's work through Jesus's word
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by a word alone. The passive points to God as the one who restores.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
records.gloss: Having gone out but the Pharisees counsel took against him how him they might destroy.
pieces: The Pharisees left and met together to plot against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, looking for a way to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.

L.14: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, how they might destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.14: Then the Pharisees went out and met together. They made plans to kill Jesus.

decisions.choice: destroy: kill
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Herod seeking to kill the child Jesus (2:13). This is the first plot against Jesus's life by the leaders.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

records.source: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν.
records.gloss: The but Jesus having known withdrew from there.
pieces: Jesus knew what they were planning, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew from there.

L.15: But Jesus, knowing [it], withdrew from there.

R.15: Jesus knew about their plan, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away from danger
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this verb when Jesus or his family moves away from a threat (2:14, 22; 4:12; 14:13).

decisions.choice: what they were planning (B); about their plan (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Jesus knew.

records.heading: God's chosen servant

records.source: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας, καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
records.gloss: And followed him many, and he healed them all, \v 16 and he warned them that not known him they should make, \v 17 so that might be fulfilled the spoken through Isaiah the prophet saying,
pieces: Many people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed every one of them.
But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them not to tell others who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.
This was so that the word spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled:

L.15: And many followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them all,
L.16: and warned them that they should not make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known,
L.17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,

R.15: Many people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed all of them.
R.16: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} warned them not to tell anyone about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.17: This made what the prophet Isaiah had said come true:

decisions.choice: not to make him known: Jesus does not seek fame
alternatives: he wanted to keep the healings secret from the Pharisees only
decisions.reason: Matthew explains the command by the quotation that follows: God's servant does not shout or push himself forward (12:19).

decisions.choice: many, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: many crowds, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "many crowds". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 8:17
decisions.reason: The formula that introduces a fulfilled prophecy is given in the same words each time.

records.source: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου εἰς ὃν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.
records.gloss: Behold the servant of me whom I chose, the beloved of me in whom was well pleased the soul of me; I will put the Spirit of me upon him, and justice to the Gentiles he will proclaim.
pieces: "See {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, the one I have chosen, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved one, in whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul delights. I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make justice known to the Gentiles.

L.18: "Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant whom I have chosen, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} beloved in whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul is well pleased; I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.

R.18: "Here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will announce justice to people of every nation.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 42:1-4: the servant of the LORD
alternatives: a general saying about God's people
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes the passage in a form of his own, close to neither the Hebrew nor the Greek Old Testament throughout. Where Isaiah has "my chosen", Matthew has "my beloved", the word of the voice at Jesus's baptism (3:17; see 17:5).

decisions.choice: servant: the servant of God in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. Isaiah's servant is meant, and Matthew sees him in Jesus.

decisions.choice: justice: the right order God establishes
decisions.reason: The word can mean judgment. In Isaiah 42 it is the just rule the servant brings, even to the nations.

decisions.choice: spans on "my" for God and on "he" and "him" for the servant
decisions.reason: God speaks here, and the servant is Jesus, so the pronouns for both take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: look (L), here is (B, R); Gentiles (L, B), people of every nation (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the servant as a herald would. Readable says who the Gentiles are.

records.source: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Not will he quarrel nor cry out, nor will hear anyone in the streets the voice of him.
pieces: He will not quarrel or shout; no one will hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} raising {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice in the streets.

L.19: He will not quarrel nor shout, nor will anyone hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice in the broad streets.

R.19: He will not argue with people or shout at them. No one will hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} shouting in the streets.

decisions.choice: quarrel, cry out: the servant does not fight or push himself forward
decisions.reason: Matthew sees this in Jesus's withdrawal and his command not to make him known (12:15-16).

decisions.choice: the streets: the wide, public streets of a town
decisions.reason: The word means the broad streets where people gathered and speakers drew crowds.

records.source: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.
records.gloss: A reed bruised not he will break and a wick smoldering not he will quench, until he brings out to victory the justice.
pieces: He will not snap off a bent reed or snuff out a wick that is barely burning, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has led justice on to victory.

L.20: A crushed reed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not break, and a smoldering wick {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not put out, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings justice forth to victory.

R.20: He will not break off a reed that is bent. He will not put out a lamp wick that is barely burning. He will be like this until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes justice win.

decisions.choice: the crushed reed and the smoldering wick: people who are weak and failing
decisions.reason: The servant does not finish off those who are bent or almost spent. He is gentle with them (see 11:28-29).

decisions.choice: until he brings justice to victory: Isaiah 42:3-4 in brief
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the servant will bring out justice faithfully and not grow faint until he has set justice in the earth. Matthew sums this up.

decisions.choice: victory: success, the final triumph of justice
decisions.reason: The servant's gentleness is not weakness; justice will win in the end.

decisions.choice: He will be like this until
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and joins the last clause to what comes before.

records.source: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
records.gloss: And in the name of him Gentiles will hope.
pieces: And the Gentiles will put their hope in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."

L.21: And in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name [the] Gentiles will hope."

R.21: People of every nation will put their hope in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: the Gentiles will hope in his name: Isaiah 42:4 in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Here Matthew follows the Greek Old Testament. The Hebrew says the coastlands will wait for his teaching.

decisions.choice: his name: the servant himself, all that he is
decisions.reason: To hope in someone's name is to hope in that person.

decisions.choice: in him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

records.source: Τότε προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.
records.gloss: Then was brought to him a demon-possessed blind and mute; and he healed him, so that the mute to speak and to see.
pieces: Then a man under the power of a demon was brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The man was blind and unable to speak. Jesus healed him, and now the man could speak and see.

L.22: Then a demon-possessed [man], blind and mute, was brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed him, so that the mute [man] spoke and saw.

R.22: Then some people brought a man to Jesus. A demon was controlling the man, and he was blind and could not talk. Jesus healed him, and the man was able to talk and to see.

decisions.choice: demon-possessed: under a demon's control
decisions.reason: As in 9:32-33, Matthew links the man's blindness and muteness with the demon.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak
decisions.reason: The word can mean deaf or mute. Here it means mute, since healing lets him speak.

decisions.choice: some people brought
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive active.

records.heading: By the Spirit of God

records.source: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον· Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυίδ;
records.gloss: And were amazed all the crowds and were saying, Not this is the son of David?
pieces: The crowds were all beside themselves. "Might this man be the Son of David?" they asked.

L.23: And all the crowds were amazed and were saying, "This is not the Son of David, is it?"

R.23: All the people were amazed. They said, "Could this man be the Son of David, the king God promised?"

decisions.choice: a hesitant question
decisions.reason: The question is framed as if expecting "no", but it shows that the crowds are beginning to wonder.

decisions.choice: Son of David: a title for the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names the Messiah (1:1).

decisions.choice: the king God promised
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means.

records.source: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον· Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.
records.gloss: The but Pharisees having heard said, This one not casts out the demons except by the Beelzebul ruler of the demons.
pieces: But the Pharisees heard it and said, "This man drives out demons only with the help of Beelzebul, the prince of demons."

L.24: But when the Pharisees heard [it], they said, "This [man] does not cast out the demons except by Beelzebul, [the] ruler of the demons."

R.24: But the Pharisees heard what the people were saying. They said, "This man makes demons leave only by the power of Beelzebul. Beelzebul is the ruler of the demons."

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: a name for Satan
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charge as one about Satan (12:26). The name recalls Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2), and Jesus has already said that his opponents call him Beelzebul (10:25).

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early Greek manuscripts spell the name Beezebul. The form Beelzebub, familiar from older translations, comes from the Latin and Syriac traditions and 2 Kings 1:2. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by: by the power of
decisions.reason: The Pharisees say Satan is the power at work in Jesus.

records.source: εἰδὼς δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.
records.gloss: Having known but the thoughts of them he said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself not will stand.
pieces: Jesus knew what they were thinking, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Any kingdom that is split into warring parts falls into ruin, and any town or family that fights against itself will not last.

L.25: But knowing their thoughts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.

R.25: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "A kingdom that fights against itself will be destroyed. A town or a family that fights against itself will fall apart.

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: as in 9:4
decisions.reason: Jesus knows what they think, as God knows the heart.

decisions.choice: house: a household or family
decisions.reason: The word means the people who live together in a house.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer begins a long speech, so Balanced and Readable name him.

records.source: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: And if the Satan the Satan casts out, against himself he is divided; how then will stand the kingdom of him?
pieces: So if Satan is throwing Satan out, he has turned against himself. In that case, how could his kingdom survive?

L.26: And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?

R.26: If Satan forces out his own demons, then he is fighting against himself. How could his kingdom last?

decisions.choice: Satan casting out Satan: Satan driving out his own servants
decisions.reason: If the demons are Satan's servants, driving them out would mean Satan fighting himself.

decisions.choice: his own demons
decisions.reason: Readable says what the second "Satan" means.

records.source: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν;
records.gloss: And if I by Beelzebul cast out the demons, the sons of you by whom do they cast out?
pieces: And if I drive out demons with Beelzebul's help, then whose help do your own people use when they drive them out?

L.27: And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast [them] out?

R.27: You say that I force out demons by the power of Beelzebul. Then by whose power do your own followers force them out?

decisions.choice: your sons: your own people, your followers
decisions.reason: "Sons" can mean members or followers of a group. Some Jews of the time drove out demons (Acts 19:13).

decisions.choice: your own people (B); your own followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: You say that
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the Pharisees' own claim; Readable says so.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: Because of this they judges will be of you.
pieces: So they will be the ones to judge you.

L.27: Because of this, they will be your judges.

R.27: So your own followers will show that you are wrong.

decisions.choice: judges: they will show that your charge is false
decisions.reason: Their own exorcists show the charge to be unfair, and so they condemn it.

decisions.choice: will show that you are wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says how they will judge.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: If but by Spirit of God I cast out the demons, then has come upon you the kingdom of the God.
pieces: But if I am driving out demons by the Spirit of God, then God's kingdom has already arrived among you.

L.28: But if I cast out the demons by [the] Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

R.28: But suppose I am forcing out demons by the power of God's Spirit. That means God's kingdom has come to you.

decisions.choice: has come upon you: has already arrived
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrive or reach. Elsewhere the kingdom "has come near" (3:2; 4:17); here Jesus says it is already at work among them.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: Matthew's usual "kingdom of heaven" in other words
decisions.reason: Matthew nearly always says "kingdom of heaven", but here and in a few other places "kingdom of God" (19:24; 21:31, 43).

decisions.choice: by the Spirit of God: the Spirit God put on his servant
decisions.reason: The quotation in 12:18 said God would put his Spirit on his servant (see 3:16).

records.source: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν;
records.gloss: Or how is able anyone to enter into the house of the strong and the goods of him to plunder, if not first he binds the strong?
pieces: Or how could anyone break into the house of a strong man and make off with his goods, without tying the strong man up first?

L.29: Or how can anyone enter the house of the strong [man] and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong [man]?

R.29: Suppose someone wants to go into a strong man's house and take away his things. First he must tie up the strong man.

decisions.choice: the strong man: Satan; binding him: Jesus overpowering him
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures his casting out of demons as the defeat of Satan. Isaiah 49:24-25 asks whether captives can be taken from the mighty, and God answers that they will be.

decisions.choice: his goods: the people Satan has held captive
decisions.reason: In the picture, the goods taken from the strong man are those Jesus sets free.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable states the point.

records.source: καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.
records.gloss: And then the house of him he will plunder.
pieces: Only then can he strip the house bare.

L.29: And then he will plunder his house.

R.29: Then he can take everything in the house.

decisions.choice: and then: only after the strong man is bound
decisions.reason: The order matters: the binding comes first, then the plundering.

records.source: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
records.gloss: The not being with me against me is, and the not gathering with me scatters.
pieces: Anyone who does not stand with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stands against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Anyone who does not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gather is scattering.

L.30: The one who is not with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who does not gather with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} scatters.

R.30: If people are not on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side, they are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If they do not help {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} bring people together, they are driving people away.

decisions.choice: gather, scatter: the picture of a flock or a harvest
decisions.reason: Jesus gathers God's scattered sheep (9:36-38; Ezekiel 34:12-13). Those who do not help him work against him.

decisions.choice: no neutral ground
alternatives: a rebuke for the disciples only
decisions.reason: In the fight between God's kingdom and Satan's, no one can stand aside.

decisions.choice: bring people together
decisions.reason: Readable says what is gathered.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
records.gloss: Because of this I say to you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to men, the but of the Spirit blasphemy not will be forgiven.
pieces: This is why I tell you that people can be forgiven every sin and every slander, but no one will be forgiven for blasphemy against the Spirit.

L.31: Because of this I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to {{gender:people|men}}, but the blasphemy [against] the Spirit will not be forgiven.

R.31: So I tell you this: God will forgive people for every sin and for every evil thing they say against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But God will not forgive anyone who speaks evil against the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: blasphemy against the Spirit: calling the Spirit's work in Jesus the work of Satan
alternatives: any careless word about the Spirit
decisions.reason: The saying answers the charge of 12:24. Jesus drives out demons by the Spirit of God (12:28), and the Pharisees call it Satan's work (see Mark 3:30).

decisions.choice: blasphemy: slander, especially against God
decisions.reason: The word means speaking evil of someone. Most often in the Bible it is speech against God.

decisions.choice: will be forgiven: by God
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the one who forgives.

decisions.choice: God will forgive; the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names who forgives and which Spirit is meant (12:32).

records.source: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.
records.gloss: And whoever if speaks a word against the Son of the Man, it will be forgiven him; whoever but speaks against the Spirit the Holy, not it will be forgiven him neither in this the age nor in the coming.
pieces: A person who says something against the Son of Man may be forgiven. But a person who speaks against the Holy Spirit will find no forgiveness, not in the present age and not in the age that is coming.

L.32: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the [age] to come.

R.32: People who say something bad against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But people who speak against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. They will not be forgiven now or in the time to come.

decisions.choice: against the Son of Man, against the Spirit: misjudging Jesus can be forgiven; calling God's plain work evil shuts out forgiveness
alternatives: the Spirit is greater than the Son
a sin a believer may commit by accident
decisions.reason: People may misjudge Jesus in his humble state and later turn. Those who see the Spirit's work and call it Satan's refuse the very forgiveness God offers. The saying is hard, and its exact scope is debated.

decisions.choice: neither in this age nor in the coming one: never
decisions.reason: Jews of the time spoke of this age and the age to come. To say "neither" is to say "never".

decisions.choice: never; now or in the time to come
alternatives: in this age or the coming age
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning and keeps the two times.

records.source: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.
records.gloss: Either make the tree good and the fruit of it good, or make the tree bad and the fruit of it bad; by for the fruit the tree is known.
pieces: Either count the tree good and its fruit good, or count the tree rotten and its fruit rotten. For the fruit shows what kind of tree it is.

L.33: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for by the fruit the tree is known.

R.33: A good tree gives good fruit, and a bad tree gives bad fruit. You cannot have it both ways. People know what a tree is like by looking at its fruit.

decisions.choice: make: count, judge to be
decisions.reason: Jesus asks them to judge consistently. A good deed such as setting a man free cannot come from an evil source.

decisions.choice: the tree is known by its fruit: as in 7:16-20
decisions.reason: Jesus used the same picture of false prophets. Here it applies both to his own deeds and to the Pharisees' words (12:34-37).

decisions.choice: rotten: bad, worthless
decisions.reason: The word means rotten and so useless.

decisions.choice: You cannot have it both ways
decisions.reason: Readable says what "either ... or" demands.

records.source: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες;
records.gloss: Offspring of vipers, how are you able good things to speak evil being?
pieces: You family of snakes! How could good words come from you, since you are evil?

L.34: Offspring of vipers! How can you speak good things, being evil?

R.34: You are like a family of poisonous snakes! You are evil, so how can you say good things?

decisions.choice: offspring of vipers: John the Baptist's words (3:7)
decisions.reason: Jesus uses John's words for the leaders. The wording is the same as in 3:7 at each level.

records.source: ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.
records.gloss: Out of for the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
pieces: The mouth speaks what spills over from the heart.

L.34: For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.

R.34: What people say shows what is in their hearts.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where thoughts and choices begin
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is the center of a person's thinking and will.

decisions.choice: What people say shows what is in their hearts
alternatives: out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the proverb plainly.

records.source: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.
records.gloss: The good man out of the good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings out evil things.
pieces: From a good storehouse a good person draws out good things; from an evil storehouse an evil person draws out evil things.

L.35: The good {{gender:person|man}} out of the good treasure brings out good things, and the evil {{gender:person|man}} out of the evil treasure brings out evil things.

R.35: Good people have good things stored in their hearts, so they bring out good things. Evil people have evil things stored in their hearts, so they bring out evil things.

decisions.choice: treasure: a storehouse, here the heart
decisions.reason: The word means a treasure or the place where it is kept. The heart is meant (12:34; 6:21).

decisions.choice: stored in their hearts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the storehouse is.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·
records.gloss: I say but to you that every word careless which will speak men, they will give about it an account in day of judgment;
pieces: And I tell you this: every idle word people speak is a word they will have to answer for on judgment day.

L.36: But I tell you that every careless word that {{gender:people|men}} will speak, they will give an account of it on [the] day of judgment.

R.36: I tell you that on the day when God judges people, they will have to explain every careless word they have said.

decisions.choice: careless: idle, useless, spoken without thought
decisions.reason: The word means idle or useless. Even words spoken without care show what is in the heart.

decisions.choice: give an account: answer for, as before a judge
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of settling accounts and of answering for one's actions.

decisions.choice: the day when God judges people
decisions.reason: Readable says who judges.

records.source: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.
records.gloss: By for the words of you you will be justified, and by the words of you you will be condemned.
pieces: Your own words will declare you innocent, or your own words will condemn you."

L.37: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned."

R.37: The words you say will show whether you are right with God or guilty before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: justified: declared in the right at the judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is set against "condemned", so it means acquitted by the judge.

decisions.choice: your: singular
decisions.reason: Jesus turns to each person: every one will answer for his or her own words.

decisions.choice: declare you innocent (B); right with God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being justified means here.

records.source: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν.
records.gloss: Then answered him some of the scribes and Pharisees saying, Teacher, we want from you a sign to see.
pieces: At this some of the scribes and Pharisees spoke up. "Teacher," they said, "we would like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to show us a sign."

L.38: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.38: Then some teachers of the law and Pharisees said to Jesus, "Teacher, we want {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to show us a sign that proves God sent {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: sign: a miracle from God that would prove Jesus's authority
decisions.reason: They have just seen a healing. They ask for a sign of their own choosing, one that would settle the matter (16:1).

decisions.choice: answered: responded to what Jesus had just said
decisions.reason: "Answered" often means simply "spoke up" in reply to a situation.

decisions.choice: a sign that proves God sent you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign was meant to show.

records.heading: The sign of Jonah

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου.
records.gloss: He but answering said to them, A generation evil and adulterous a sign seeks, and a sign not will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
pieces: He answered them, "An evil, unfaithful generation goes looking for a sign, but the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah the prophet.

L.39: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

R.39: Jesus answered, "The people of today are evil and are not faithful to God. They ask for a sign. But no sign will be given to them except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

decisions.choice: adulterous: unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel's turning from God adultery (Hosea 2:2; Jeremiah 3:8).

decisions.choice: generation: the people living at this time
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of his own generation (11:16).

decisions.choice: unfaithful (B); not faithful to God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the word means here.

records.source: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας.
records.gloss: Just as for was Jonah in the belly of the sea creature three days and three nights, so will be the Son of the Man in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
pieces: Jonah spent three days and three nights inside the great sea creature, and in the same way the Son of Man will spend three days and three nights deep in the earth.

L.40: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

R.40: Jonah was inside a huge fish for three days and three nights. In the same way, the Son of Man will be in the grave for three days and three nights.

decisions.choice: Jonah in the sea creature: Jonah 1:17 (2:1 in the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: Matthew's words follow the Greek Old Testament of that verse.

decisions.choice: sea monster: a huge sea creature
decisions.reason: The word means a large sea creature. Jonah's Hebrew says "a great fish".

decisions.choice: three days and three nights: a way of counting parts of three days
decisions.reason: Jews counted part of a day as a day (compare 1 Samuel 30:12-13; Esther 4:16 with 5:1). Jesus was buried on Friday and rose on Sunday, "on the third day" (16:21).

decisions.choice: the heart of the earth: the grave, the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Jonah too speaks of being in the depths and the place of the dead (Jonah 2:2-6).

decisions.choice: in the grave
alternatives: in the heart of the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

records.source: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
records.gloss: Men Ninevites will rise up in the judgment with the generation this and will condemn it; because they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, greater than Jonah here.
pieces: On judgment day the people of Nineveh will stand up alongside this generation and condemn it. They turned from their sins when Jonah preached. Yet here is something greater than Jonah.

L.41: {{gender:People|Men}} of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and look, [something] greater than Jonah [is] here.

R.41: On judgment day, the people of Nineveh will stand up beside the people of today and show that they are guilty. The people of Nineveh turned from their sins when Jonah preached to them. But here is something greater than Jonah!

decisions.choice: they repented at Jonah's preaching: Jonah 3:5-10
decisions.reason: The whole city of Nineveh turned from its evil ways when Jonah warned it.

decisions.choice: rise up with this generation and condemn it: stand as witnesses at the judgment
alternatives: come back to life to punish them
decisions.reason: The people of Nineveh will be like witnesses in a court. Their response shows how guilty this generation is.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter, as in 12:6
decisions.reason: It points to Jesus and what God is doing through him.

decisions.choice: look (L); yet (B); but (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
records.gloss: Queen of south will be raised in the judgment with the generation this and will condemn it; because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, greater than Solomon here.
pieces: The queen from the south will stand up on judgment day alongside this generation and condemn it. She traveled from the far edges of the earth to listen to Solomon's wisdom. Yet here is something greater than Solomon.

L.42: [The] queen of [the] south will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, [something] greater than Solomon [is] here.

R.42: On judgment day, the queen from the south will stand up beside the people of today and show that they are guilty. She came from a land far away to listen to Solomon's wise teaching. But here is something greater than Solomon!

decisions.choice: the queen of the south: the queen of Sheba, 1 Kings 10:1-13
decisions.reason: She came from far to the south to test Solomon's wisdom and praised the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: the ends of the earth: a very distant land
alternatives: the literal edge of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses how far she traveled to hear wisdom.

decisions.choice: look (L); yet (B); but (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει.
records.gloss: When but the unclean spirit goes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finds.
pieces: When an unclean spirit leaves a person, it wanders through dry country in search of a place to rest, but it finds none.

L.43: Now when the unclean spirit goes out from the {{gender:person|man}}, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find [it].

R.43: When an evil spirit comes out of a person, it goes through dry, empty places. It looks for a place to rest, but it does not find one.

decisions.choice: waterless places: the desert, thought of as a home of evil spirits
decisions.reason: The prophets picture ruined, desert places as haunted by wild creatures and spirits (Isaiah 13:21; 34:14).

decisions.choice: unclean: impure, opposed to God's holiness
decisions.reason: Matthew uses "unclean spirit" for a demon (10:1).

decisions.choice: evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain term.

records.heading: The unclean spirit returns

records.source: τότε λέγει· Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον· καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σχολάζοντα σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
records.gloss: Then it says, Into the house of me I will return from where I came out; and having come it finds unoccupied, swept and put in order.
pieces: So it says, 'I will go back to the home I came out of.' It returns and finds the place standing empty, swept, and set in order.

L.44: Then it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.' And when it comes, it finds [it] unoccupied, swept, and put in order.

R.44: Then it says, 'I will go back to the home I left.' So it goes back and finds that home empty. It has been swept clean and made neat.

decisions.choice: my house: the person the spirit left
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks of the person as its home.

decisions.choice: unoccupied: empty, with nothing in the spirit's place
decisions.reason: The house is clean but empty. Nothing has filled it, so the spirit can return.

records.source: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτὰ ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ· καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
records.gloss: Then it goes and takes with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and having entered they dwell there; and becomes the last of the man that worse than the first.
pieces: Then it goes off and brings back seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they move in and settle there. In the end that person is worse off than at the start.

L.45: Then it goes and takes along with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and live there; and the last [state] of that {{gender:person|man}} becomes worse than the first.

R.45: Then the spirit goes and brings back seven other spirits. They are even more evil than it is. They all go into the person and live there. So that person is in a worse condition than before.

decisions.choice: seven: a full number
decisions.reason: Seven often stands for completeness. The person is wholly taken over.

decisions.choice: the last things, the first: the person's final state and earlier state
decisions.reason: The neuter plural speaks of the person's condition.

decisions.choice: worse off than at the start (B); in a worse condition than before (R)
alternatives: the last state becomes worse than the first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

records.source: οὕτως ἔσται καὶ τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρᾷ.
records.gloss: So it will be also to the generation this the evil.
pieces: And this evil generation will fare the same way."

L.45: So it will be also with this evil generation."

R.45: That is what will happen to the evil people living today."

decisions.choice: this generation: freed from demons by Jesus, but not filled with God's kingdom
alternatives: only a story about one person
decisions.reason: Jesus has been driving out demons among them (12:22-28). If they reject him, their end will be worse than their beginning.

records.source: Ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος τοῖς ὄχλοις ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἱστήκεισαν ἔξω ζητοῦντες αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι.
records.gloss: Still him speaking to the crowds behold, the mother and the brothers of him were standing outside seeking to him to speak.
pieces: Jesus was still talking to the crowds when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and brothers arrived. They stood outside, hoping for a word with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.46: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking to the crowds, look, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.46: Jesus was still talking to the crowds. Meanwhile, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and brothers were standing outside. They wanted to talk to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: brothers: Jesus's brothers, named in 13:55
decisions.reason: The word normally means brothers. Christian traditions differ on whether they were sons of Mary and Joseph or close relatives.

decisions.choice: were standing outside: outside the house or the crowd
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say where Jesus was speaking. The family could not reach him.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Those who do the Father's will

records.source: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ἑστήκασιν, ζητοῦντές σοι λαλῆσαι.
records.gloss: Said but someone to him, Behold, the mother of you and the brothers of you outside are standing, seeking to you to speak.
pieces: Someone told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother and brothers are standing out there. They are asking to speak with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.47: And someone said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.47: Someone said to Jesus, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside. They want to talk to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: the verse is present, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is missing in some important early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, lack this verse. It may have been added to explain "the one telling him" in 12:48, or lost when a copyist's eye skipped from "to speak" at the end of 12:46 to the same words at the end of 12:47. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); look (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ λέγοντι αὐτῷ· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου, καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;
records.gloss: He but answering said to the one telling him, Who is the mother of me, and who are the brothers of me?
pieces: Jesus answered the one who had told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother? And who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"

L.48: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to the one telling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother, and who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"

R.48: Jesus answered him, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother? Who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"

decisions.choice: who is my mother: a question Jesus answers himself
decisions.reason: Jesus asks in order to give the answer in 12:49-50.

records.source: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·
records.gloss: And having stretched out the hand of him toward the disciples of him he said, Behold, the mother of me and the brothers of me;
pieces: He held out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand toward {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. "Look," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "these are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers.

L.49: And stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand toward {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers!

R.49: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pointed to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and said, "Look! These people are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers.

decisions.choice: his disciples: those who follow him
decisions.reason: The word can include more than the twelve. Jesus points to those who are with him as learners.

decisions.choice: stretching out his hand: a gesture that points
decisions.reason: The gesture shows whom he means.

decisions.choice: look at every level
decisions.reason: Jesus points to people before him, so the word is kept in his speech.

records.source: ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, αὐτός μου ἀδελφὸς καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
records.gloss: Whoever for shall do the will of the Father of me who in heavens, he of me brother and sister and mother is.
pieces: For anyone who does the will of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven is a brother and sister and mother to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.50: For whoever does the will of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in [the] heavens, {{gender:that one|he}} is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brother and sister and mother."

R.50: Anyone who does what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven wants is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sister and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother."

decisions.choice: doing the Father's will: what makes someone Jesus's family
decisions.reason: Those who do the will of the Father belong to Jesus's family (see 7:21).

decisions.choice: sister: women belong to this family too
decisions.reason: No sister was named at the door, but Jesus includes sisters among those who do God's will.

decisions.choice: to me
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the relationship at the end for a natural sentence.
